identifiers.title: HEART
identifiers.definition: The parent profile of HEART (Hypermedia Engine for Agentic Resource Transitions). A response names it beside the concrete dialect profile, in Link: rel="profile". It is never negotiated alone. A client that knows it knows that the response follows HEART's rules: state and legal acts in one representation, acts conditional on the representation's validator, and shared layers checked by integrity.

identifiers.title: HAL Schema Forms, HEART profile
identifiers.definition: HAL Schema Forms (https://github.com/jbadeau/hal-schema-forms) with HEART's additions: template pointers, integrity on shared links, schemas by $ref, forms named by link relation and described by ALPS, and refusals as problem details. An L0 response stays valid upstream HAL Schema Forms. Media type application/hal+json.

identifiers.title: HAL-FORMS, HEART on-ramp
identifiers.definition: HAL-FORMS (application/prs.hal-forms+json) as HEART's on-ramp dialect, served at L0 only. Its templates are keyed by act name, and it is computed from the same legality decision as HAL Schema Forms, so both dialects always offer the same acts.

identifiers.title: forms
identifiers.definition: Links a resource's state (Layer 1) to its affordance set: the forms legal in its current state, shared by every resource in that state. The link carries integrity, a W3C Subresource Integrity value, and the client checks the set's bytes against it before use. Written as the CURIE hr:forms.

identifiers.title: unavailable
identifiers.definition: Links to a list of the acts that are not offered in this state, each with the server's reason. A client fetches it only when someone asks why an act is missing, checks it against the link's integrity, and never acts on what it lists. Written as the CURIE hr:unavailable.

identifiers.title: form
identifiers.definition: From an act's target to its form, where the form already lives: in the owning resource's shared affordance set, by a JSON Pointer fragment, with the set's integrity and the form's own. Served on the act's target when it is read, so the target has a representation of its own while the form stays shared. Written as the CURIE hr:form.

identifiers.title: affordances
identifiers.definition: From a service's index to its affordances: every form the service can offer, keyed by the form's integrity (hr:integrity) as the index's hr:manifest names it, each with its relation and a describedby link to the JSON Schema it uses where that schema is served apart. A client that meets an integrity it has not seen follows links from the index to the schema and never knows a schema's address in advance. Read with GET; revalidated with its ETag; open to the same callers as the index. Written as the CURIE hr:affordances.

identifiers.title: keys
identifiers.definition: To the JWK Set (RFC 7517, application/jwk-set+json) of Ed25519 keys (RFC 8037) that the linking party signs with, by key id. A service that signs links it from its index and serves it open to every caller, cached a day. In a RISE request's envelope it names the keys the caller signed the request with; on a watch it names the keys the service signs its answers with, the ones the caller checks them by. A verifier takes keys only from the link of the resource it trusts, never from a link the signed message carries. Written as the CURIE hr:keys.

identifiers.title: reply-to
identifiers.definition: In a RISE request's envelope, the caller's own reply resource: where the service answers later, by the reply's forms. Its type and profile say how to read the reply. Required with hr:keys in the envelope of a request such as a library's tell-me-when-renewable. A watch the request brings into being links it too. Written as the CURIE hr:reply-to.

identifiers.title: progress
identifiers.definition: On a reply, while it awaits: report how far the work has got. A PATCH of the reply itself, application/merge-patch+json, with If-Match the reply's ETag, signed (RFC 9421, with Content-Digest). Minimum schema: state, the const awaiting; percent, an integer from 0 to 100; note, a string or null, where a note left out stays and null clears it; _links with hr:in-reply-to. 200 with the reply; 401 unsigned or badly signed; 409 not offered once the reply is answered, or link-conflict for another request; 412 stale; 422 invalid. Each progress is a change and is recorded in the reply's version-history. Written as the CURIE hr:progress.

identifiers.title: completed
identifiers.definition: On a reply, while it awaits: send the result; the reply is answered, at 100 percent, with no note unless one is sent. A PATCH of the reply itself, application/merge-patch+json, with If-Match, signed. Minimum schema: state, the const completed; result, in the shape the reply's owner names in its schema; _links with hr:in-reply-to. Replay: the same result sent again after the answer is answered 200 with the same ETag and records nothing; a different one is 409 not-offered. Other answers: 401, 412, 422 as for progress. The answered reply offers no forms and says why in hr:unavailable. Written as the CURIE hr:completed.

identifiers.title: failed
identifiers.definition: On a reply, while it awaits: say the work failed. A PATCH of the reply itself whose body is an RFC 9457 problem document, application/problem+json, with If-Match, signed. Minimum schema: state, the const failed; type, a URI; title; detail, optional; _links with hr:in-reply-to. The reply is answered and keeps the problem under _embedded.problem, so its owner sees why. A body sent as merge-patch is refused 415 with Accept-Patch. Written as the CURIE hr:failed.

identifiers.title: in-reply-to
identifiers.definition: From an answer, and from the reply it lands on, to the request it answers: the absolute address of the watch whose 201 created it. The service sends it in each answer's _links; the reply keeps the first one and links it in every state after. An answer that names another request is refused 409 link-conflict and changes nothing. Trust rule: it must equal the Location of the 201 the caller received, and the caller checks answers' signatures with keys from that watch's hr:keys, never from a link the signer supplied. Written as the CURIE hr:in-reply-to.

identifiers.title: cancel
identifiers.definition: On a RISE request's watch, while it awaits its answer: withdraw it, so no answer will come. A PATCH of the watch itself, application/merge-patch+json, with If-Match, whose standing is the const cancelled. 200 with the watch, cancelled. Once the service has answered, the watch offers no hr:cancel, its hr:unavailable says why, and a cancel sent anyway is 409 not-offered. A domain whose acts have side effects offers a compensating form here instead. Written as the CURIE hr:cancel.

identifiers.title: integrity
identifiers.definition: A form's own integrity: over what the form does, its target, template pointers, method, content type and its schema's integrity, in canonical form; not its title or description. On every form, the index's among them, so a client that pins a form notices when what it does changes. Written hr:integrity.

identifiers.title: manifest
identifiers.definition: A member of a service's index: by relation, the integrity of every form the service can offer, the index's own and every resource type's acts, and a digest over that list that changes when any form does. Known from the declarations, with nothing read. hr:affordances lists the same forms by integrity, with the way to each schema. Written hr:manifest.

identifiers.title: A signature is required
identifiers.definition: 401: the act carries no signature where the resource takes only signed acts (RFC 9421 over Content-Digest, RFC 9530). The answer says how to sign: WWW-Authenticate names the Signature scheme, declared by the HAL Schema Forms profile, and Accept-Signature names the components, @method, @target-uri, content-digest and if-match, and the key id to sign with.

identifiers.title: The signature does not verify
identifiers.definition: 401: the act carries a signature, but it does not verify by the key it names, from the keys the resource trusts for it: the body was changed after signing, or another key made it. The answer carries WWW-Authenticate and Accept-Signature, as for signature-required.

identifiers.title: The act names another resource than the state keeps
identifiers.definition: 409: the act names, under the relation in rel, another resource than the one the resource already keeps there, such as an answer on a reply that names another request than the one the reply answers. Nothing changes.

identifiers.title: The body is not of a type the act takes
identifiers.definition: 415: the act's body is of another type than the act takes, such as a failure sent as merge-patch rather than as a problem document. accepted lists the types the resource takes, as does Accept-Patch (RFC 5789) for a PATCH, or Accept-Post for a POST.

identifiers.title: Accept names no format this server produces
identifiers.definition: 406: Accept names none of the formats a resource is served in. alternates lists them, each its media type and, where it has one, its profile: HAL Schema Forms, HAL-FORMS, HTML and plain JSON. Every answer names the same formats as alternate links.

identifiers.title: The act is stale: the state has changed
identifiers.definition: 412. The act's If-Match no longer names the resource's current representation: someone else changed it first. The client re-reads the resource and decides again. It never resends the act.

identifiers.title: The act is not offered in the resource's current state
identifiers.definition: 409. The act is not legal in the resource's current state, however current the client's view. The client re-reads, and does not retry.

identifiers.title: The body does not match the form's schema
identifiers.definition: 422. The body breaks the form's JSON Schema. The problem lists each violation with a JSON Pointer. Not retried.

identifiers.title: A rule of the resource refuses the act
identifiers.definition: 422. The body satisfies the schema, but a rule of the resource that the schema cannot express refuses it, in the rule's own words, with a JSON Pointer. Not retried.

identifiers.title: If-Match is required
identifiers.definition: 428. An act was sent without If-Match. Every HEART act is conditional on the representation the client read.

identifiers.title: A credential is needed
identifiers.definition: 401. The resource needs a Basic or Bearer credential the service admits; the response offers a WWW-Authenticate challenge for each. A wrong credential is answered exactly as a missing one.

identifiers.title: The HEART specification
identifiers.definition: The specification a service's home document names as describedBy.

identifiers.title: Home document variables
identifiers.definition: The home document names each template variable by a URI under /vars/: {noun}-id and {noun}-name, such as /vars/bed-id. Each is the identifier, or the name, of one resource of the type the noun names.
